title: Electronic Microprocessor/Microcontroller Design
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 30S/45Q to fewer than 60S/90Q units

program.section_heading: Electronic Microprocessor/Microcontroller Design - Certificate of Achievement: City
outcomes: Students who complete the program will be able to demonstrate the proper use of basic electronic test instrumentation including an oscilloscope, a digital volt-ohm meter, a signal generator, and a dual power supply.
Students who complete the program will be able to analyze and explain basic electronic theory including Ohm’s Law, the power formula, and calculation of voltage gain and power gain.

Students who complete the program will be able to identify standard electronic components including resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, bipolar transistors, field effect transistors, and integrated circuits.
Students who complete the program will be able to demonstrate the ability to prepare reports that include text, tables, and spreadsheets using productivity software on a computer.
careers: entry-level technical positions in the microprocessor/microcontroller field

notes: Outcomes recorded are the four printed under 'Learning Outcome(s):'; the lead-in 'Students who complete the Electronic Microprocessor/Microcontroller Design Program will be able to:' was omitted, but each outcome as printed begins with its own 'Students who complete the program will be able to...' wording, kept verbatim.

The Summary also prints a 'Students who successfully complete the Certificate... are prepared to:' list of three items (interpret block diagrams; modify computer programs; develop interface circuits). These were treated as program description rather than learning outcomes; a reviewer may wish to confirm.
Block stated total and program total both taken from 'Semester Units: 37.0' and 'Total Units: 37.0'; the listed course units sum to 37.
The course descriptions section is cut off partway through ELDT 144L; descriptions for ELDT 225, 225L, 232, 232L are not in the text, but those courses appear in the requirements list.
Catalog notes that the Electronics Department requires completion of all certificate requirements within five years.
